---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {

    public List<RoleResponse> listAsOf(String sheetId, LocalDate date) {
        return listFrom(sheetId, History.asOf("sheet_role", "sheet_id, user_name", date));
    }

    private List<RoleResponse> listFrom(String sheetId, String table) {
        return jdbc.query("SELECT user_name, role FROM " + table + " WHERE sheet_id = ? ORDER BY user_name",
                (rs, i) -> new RoleResponse(rs.getString("user_name"), Role.valueOf(rs.getString("role")).shown()),
                sheetId);
    }

    /** The role the user acts in on the sheet: steward while a delegation to them is in force, else
     *  the role assigned. */
    public Role find(String sheetId, String user) {
        return delegations.delegator(sheetId, user) != null ? Role.STEWARD : assigned(sheetId, user);
    }

    /** The user's role as assigned on the sheet, delegations aside: clerk unless assigned otherwise. */
    public Role assigned(String sheetId, String user) {
        List<String> found = jdbc.queryForList("SELECT role FROM sheet_role WHERE sheet_id = ? AND user_name = ?",
                String.class, sheetId, user);
        return found.isEmpty() ? Role.CLERK : Role.valueOf(found.get(0));
    }

    /** Refuses any change to an archived sheet, and any change by a viewer: a viewer may change nothing
     *  on the sheet. */
    public void refuseChange(String sheetId, String user) throws InvalidSheetException {
        sheets.refuseArchived(sheetId);
        if (find(sheetId, user == null ? "" : user.trim()) == Role.VIEWER) {
            throw new InvalidSheetException("A viewer may change nothing");
        }
    }

    public void set(String sheetId, String user, Role role) {
        jdbc.update("MERGE INTO sheet_role (sheet_id, user_name, role) KEY (sheet_id, user_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                sheetId, user, role.name());

    public List<RoleResponse> listAsOf(String sheetId, LocalDate date) {
        return listFrom(sheetId, History.asOf("sheet_role", "sheet_id, user_name", date));
    }

    private List<RoleResponse> listFrom(String sheetId, String table) {
        return jdbc.query("SELECT user_name, role FROM " + table + " WHERE sheet_id = ? ORDER BY user_name",
                (rs, i) -> new RoleResponse(rs.getString("user_name"), Role.valueOf(rs.getString("role")).shown()),
                sheetId);
    }

    /** The role the user acts in on the sheet: steward while a delegation to them is in force, else
     *  the role assigned. */
    public Role find(String sheetId, String user) {
        return delegations.delegator(sheetId, user) != null ? Role.STEWARD : assigned(sheetId, user);
    }

    /** The user's role as assigned on the sheet, delegations aside: clerk unless assigned otherwise. */
    public Role assigned(String sheetId, String user) {
        List<String> found = jdbc.queryForList("SELECT role FROM sheet_role WHERE sheet_id = ? AND user_name = ?",
                String.class, sheetId, user);
        return found.isEmpty() ? Role.CLERK : Role.valueOf(found.get(0));
    }

    /** Refuses any change to an archived sheet, and any change by a viewer: a viewer may change nothing
     *  on the sheet. */
    public void refuseChange(String sheetId, String user) throws InvalidSheetException {
        sheets.refuseArchived(sheetId);
        if (find(sheetId, user == null ? "" : user.trim()) == Role.VIEWER) {
            throw new InvalidSheetException("A viewer may change nothing");
        }
    }

    public void set(String sheetId, String user, Role role) {
        jdbc.update("MERGE INTO sheet_role (sheet_id, user_name, role) KEY (sheet_id, user_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                sheetId, user, role.name());
    }
}

package net.officefloor.hq.app.person;

import net.officefloor.hq.app.Audit;

/** Records a stored person edit: PERSON_EDITED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> grade=<grade>, the grade
 *  in force on the sheet's today after the save, then terms=<days>, those in force on the sheet's today, when the edit
 *  changed their terms (empty when none are in force), then contact=<contact> when the edit changed their contact (empty when it cleared it). */
public class AuditPersonEdited {
    public void audit(@Val PersonRequest request, @Val Person person, @Val Rollup before, Audit audit,
            RollupService rollups, SheetStore sheets) {
        Integer terms = person.termsOn(sheets.today(person.getSheetId()));
        audit.record("PERSON_EDITED sheet=" + person.getSheetId() + " by=" + request.user() + " name="
                + person.getName() + " grade=" + person.gradeOn(sheets.today(person.getSheetId()))
                + (person.isTermsChanged() ? " terms=" + (terms == null ? "" : terms) : "")
                + (person.isContactChanged() ? " contact=" + (person.getContact() == null ? "" : person.getContact()) : ""));
        rollups.record(person.getSheetId(), request.user(), before);
    }
}

Grade merge is in place, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests.

**What it does**
- **Screen:** the Grades section has two new selects and a button (`grade-merge-from`, `grade-merge-into`, `grade-merge`). A merge that goes through shows its result in `grade-merged`, e.g. "A into B: 1 moved". A refused merge shows the existing `grade-error` element, which the retire form already used. Changing a select or pressing either button clears that error, and a successful merge re-reads the whole sheet.
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/merge` endpoint (`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/merge.POST.yml`). It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, the same grade twice, an unknown grade and an archived sheet, and writes nothing in those cases.
- **The merge itself** (`grade/MergeGrade.java`) writes `GRADE_MERGED from=… into=…` to the audit file first. It then takes everyone whose grade today is the merged grade, in list order, and gives each one the other grade from the sheet's today. It does this with the same steps as the bulk-grade action, so each person gets `PERSON_EDITED` and their rollup lines. If the target grade is retired, the merge is refused, as the person form would refuse it.
- No stored-data change was needed: the merge uses the existing grade history.

**Two things I matched to the test rather than the wording of the request:**
- **An extra rollup pair.** The test expects a second `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` pair after the per-person lines, with the same values. I made the merge record that pair for how the whole merge moved the figures, written after the per-person lines. It appears only when the merge changed a figure, which is why Cam's merge writes just `PERSON_EDITED`. That is my reading of what the test expects, not something the request spells out.
- **The result text names the grades.** It shows the grades, not just a count, because the test's two successful merges both move one person. With a count alone the second result would look the same as the first, and the test couldn't tell it finished.
